exposure: BMI at admission (< 35 kg/m² vs. >= 35 kg/m²)
cohort: The study included 273 nulliparous term patients with singleton pregnancies at a single tertiary care center, grouped by BMI at admission.
finding: Patients with obesity (BMI >= 35 kg/m²) required significantly more pushes and longer pushing duration to achieve vaginal delivery, and exceeding 115 total pushes was associated with a sixfold increase in operative delivery rates.
mod_finding: Operative and second-stage cesarean deliveries involved significantly more total pushes compared to spontaneous vaginal deliveries, with a notable increase in operative delivery once pushes exceeded 115.
